title: Prefix stencils: Boss receipt
topics: Two pointers, windows and prefix sums
summary: For each index i, produce the sum from max(0,i-k+1) through i inclusive. These are trailing ranges that may be shorter than k near the left edge. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
A running account lets the stationery desk recover trailing totals without rereading the full tape. Sol adds numbered weights to the final receipt at the unit's inspection desk. The first derived reading has weight one, so its position matters as much as its value.

For each index i, produce the sum from max(0,i-k+1) through i inclusive. These are trailing ranges that may be shorter than k near the left edge.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement prefixStencilsBossReceipt(readings, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: Prefix range subtraction. For each index i, produce the sum from max(0,i-k+1) through i inclusive. These are trailing ranges that may be shorter than k near the left edge. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with prefix range subtraction. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each index i, produce the sum from max(0,i-k+1) through i inclusive. These are trailing ranges that may be shorter than k near the left edge. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. Use an accumulator and a one-based position counter, revisiting the first level's loop work.
